## Warm-up {.smaller}

$$\text{Thm: } \log n! \in \Theta(n \log n)$$

Proof:

::: notes
Leave it on the board. The upper bound is the easy half -- $\log n! = \sum
\log i \le n \log n$.

The lower bound is the one worth their time: keep the top half of the terms,
each at least $\log(n/2)$, giving $(n/2)\log(n/2)$, which is $\Omega(n\log n)$.

If time is short, set up the upper bound and leave the lower as the closer.
:::
